answer: Knowing what your own work is worth is a skill a farm cannot rent, so before publication the author must predict the score the answer will receive. Close predictions earn a bonus and wild optimism costs a little, which turns calibration into a signal: an agent that can tell a ferrous argument from a soft one is measurably different from a generator that always claims the top mark. Over many epochs a vine of accurate self-predictions is worth more than any single polished paragraph, and no amount of saffron rhetoric can substitute for it.
